title: Concrete, checkable instructions
statement: Tell a writer in concrete, checkable terms what the item must make the student do, not in abstract labels such as a taxonomy level or 'be specific'.
detail: After several prompt runs, the AP generator's blueprint concluded that a model interprets abstract instructions differently, that 'be specific' means different things in different contexts, and that every instruction should be checkable (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/archive/RUN7_BLUEPRINT.md`). Cognitive-level labels in the prompt did not constrain what the model made and were replaced by behavioural constraints (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/archive/PROMPT_EVOLUTION.md`). The blueprint's rule is to describe the behaviour wanted, not the classification, because the model doesn't reliably map taxonomy levels to behaviours (the same blueprint).
against: The evidence compares whole runs that changed several things at once, and the blueprint itself warns that such comparisons can't isolate which change caused a regression (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/archive/RUN7_BLUEPRINT.md`).

evidence.quote: - Describe the BEHAVIOR you want, not the classification
- Model doesn't reliably map taxonomy levels to behaviors
